metadata.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Backport vllm-project/vllm#61297, #44383, #46091: whole-number integer tool arguments, zero cached tokens, empty qwen3_coder tool blocks
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Backport of three upstream vLLM fixes for the OpenAI-compatible frontend and its tool parsers, one commit each, in the same form as the earlier backports #657 (vllm-project/vllm#44082) and #1406 (vllm-project/vllm#60472). main does not have them. They are the part of a larger set on our fork that main still lacks: vllm-project/vllm#46303, #40986, #43984, #55743 and #42752 are already on main through #1317, #1309, #1308 and #1314, so they are not part of this PR. All three changes are frontend code and do not depend on the GPU; the Qwen3.8-27B release profile (vllm/sm70_profiles/qwen38_27b_nvfp4_dflash2.json) runs the code paths they fix, with --enable-auto-tool-choice, the qwen3_coder tool parser and, since #1299, --enable-prompt-tokens-details.

1. vllm-project/vllm#61297 (69d00bc26, by Yoni Gozlan), "Accept whole-number floats for integer tool arguments in the response parser". coerce_to_schema_type (vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py) tried only int() for an "integer" argument, so a value written as "3.0" or "1e3" failed there and reached the final json.loads fallback as a float (3.0). JSON Schema counts whole numbers written as floats as integers. The qwen3_coder, deepseek_v4 (through the DSML base parser), seed_oss and minimax_m2 tool parsers call this helper for non-string arguments. Upstream fixes _coerce in vllm/parser/chat_parsing/response_parser.py, which this repository does not have, so the intent is ported to coerce_to_schema_type. The integer and number branches now share one helper, _parse_finite_number: int() first, so large integers stay exact as with #1308, then float(), inf and nan rejected as with #1309, whole values returned as int. An "integer" argument accepts only a whole result; "3.5" keeps the existing json.loads fallback (3.5) instead of upstream's raw string, because this function already falls back that way for every type. The "number" branch returns the same values as before. The tests follow the upstream cases with these semantics, plus a deepseek_v4 parser test for "3.0" in batch and streaming.

2. vllm-project/vllm#44383 (42ae5e7ac, by sasindharan), "Fix --enable-prompt-tokens-details omitting zero cached tokens". With --enable-prompt-tokens-details, prompt_tokens_details was only set when num_cached_tokens was truthy, so a prompt without a prefix-cache hit, for example the first turn of a conversation, omitted the field instead of reporting cached_tokens: 0. This affects chat, completion and disagg serving (vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py, vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py, vllm/entrypoints/serve/disagg/serving.py). The patch applies unchanged. Upstream tests the disagg stream (CPU) and /v1/completions (GPU server); a chat-level test is added for the streaming path with include_usage and for the non-streaming path.

3. vllm-project/vllm#46091 (7f616c327, by Ben Browning), "[Parser] Fix empty tool block silently dropping subsequent content". In the qwen3_coder streaming parser (vllm/tool_parsers/qwen3coder_tool_parser.py), a <tool_call> block that closes without a <function= header (an empty <tool_call></tool_call>, or a malformed JSON body) left the state machine waiting for a header in that block forever. Everything after it was dropped from the stream, text and any further tool call; the non-streaming path keeps the text as content and still finds later calls. Upstream fixes its ParserEngine (a TOOL_PREAMBLE -> CONTENT transition on TOOL_END); this repository runs Qwen3CoderToolParser, so the intent is ported to its state machine. A closed block without a function header is skipped. Because current_tool_index is also the index of the emitted call, skipped blocks are counted separately (skipped_tool_blocks) and block lookups use current_tool_index plus that count, so a call after an empty block keeps index 0. Content after the skipped block is emitted, and the search for the next tool marker starts behind it. As upstream, the empty markup itself is not streamed as content. The change applies unchanged next to #1313 and #1312, which change the same parser for other cases. Beyond a literal port, the block handling of extract_tool_calls_streaming is its own method, _stream_current_tool_block, and the skip continues with the next block in the same call. Otherwise an empty block and the next call's header in one delta, followed by the rest of that call in a single delta (a call without parameters, or multi-token deltas under speculative decoding), lose the call, because an EOS delta without text does not drive the parser any further; a test covers exactly this split, with and without parameters, and its batch counterpart.

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs of this repository for 46303, 40986, 43984, 55743, 61297, 44383, 42752, 46091, cached_tokens, prompt_tokens_details, enable-prompt-tokens-details, "cached tokens", whole-number, "integer tool arguments", "integer schema", coerce_to_schema_type, "empty tool block", "tool_call block", qwen3_coder, "Qwen3 tool parser streaming", "tool_choice none", "finish_reason length tool" and "streaming error first token", and the issues for the same terms. #1317, #1309, #1308 and #1314 (merged) carry five of the upstream fixes we have on our fork, which is why those are not in this PR. #1313 and #1312 (merged) change the qwen3_coder parser for a body that completes right after its header and for response_format; #1299 (merged) turns on --enable-prompt-tokens-details in the Qwen3.8 release profile. No PR or issue covers #61297, #44383 or #46091.

AI assistance was used for this backport. I reviewed every line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3xml_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_burst_after_header.py tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_number_nonfinite.py tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_number_precision.py tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen_xml_tool_grammar.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py tests/entrypoints/serve/disagg/test_generate_stream.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_output_correctness.py tests/entrypoints/openai/test_pre_token_stream_error.py -k "not TestGPTOSSChat and not TestGPTOSSSpeculativeChat"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_seed_oss_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m2_tool_parser.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_tool_choice_none_streaming.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_error.py
The new tests against main's sources (git checkout origin/main -- vllm/ in the branch, then back): test_utils.py, test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py, test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py, test_serving_chat.py (same -k) and test_generate_stream.py.
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
End to end on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, prod-v6f 0b342e7b5, which has #61297 and #44383 but not the #46091 follow-up; DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP5 over three V100 and two RTX 8000 with --enable-prompt-tokens-details and --enable-prefix-caching): a fresh chat request of 21 prompt tokens.

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| coerce_to_schema_type (vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py), called by qwen3_coder, deepseek_v4/v32/v41, seed_oss, minimax_m2 | tool-call arguments | "integer" schema with a whole number written as a float ("3.0", "1e3") | int; fractional, non-finite and non-numeric values keep the previous fallback; "number" unchanged | executed: tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py, test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py, the qwen3coder, seed_oss and minimax_m2 parser tests | none known |
| usage.prompt_tokens_details in chat, completion and disagg serving | OpenAI usage | --enable-prompt-tokens-details, request without a prefix-cache hit (num_cached_tokens 0) | prompt_tokens_details with cached_tokens 0; nothing changes without the flag | executed: test_serving_chat.py (stream with include_usage, non-stream), test_generate_stream.py | /v1/completions server test (test_completion.py::test_single_completion) not run |
| qwen3_coder streaming parser (vllm/tool_parsers/qwen3coder_tool_parser.py) | tool calls, streaming | a <tool_call> block that closes without a <function= header, token-by-token and multi-token deltas, also with the next call's header in the same delta and its rest in the next one | block skipped; following text and calls streamed, the next call with index 0 | executed: test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py, test_qwen3coder_burst_after_header.py | a live qwen3_coder model on this code |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: always on; bug fix, not a performance change.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none (the cached-tokens fix only shows with --enable-prompt-tokens-details).
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: n/a (no benchmark; not a performance change).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: this branch on main c98a8d664; the same changes are on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, fork-main-v6 at af0072096; prod-v6f at 0b342e7b5 has all of them except the #46091 follow-up for the next call in the same delta).
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: none for the tests.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: not a performance change. The fork tree with these commits (without that #46091 follow-up) and the other upstream backports of the same bundle passed an A/B/A/B of our DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash PP5 entries against the trees without them: prefill, decode, GSM8K-30 and eight quality texts unchanged on both models (texts token-identical).
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

On this branch (main c98a8d664 + these three commits):
- First test command: 585 passed, 7 xfailed, 10 deselected (the GPT-OSS server classes), 1 failed. The failure, tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3xml_tool_parser.py::TestQwen3xmlToolParser::test_malformed_input[True], fails the same on main c98a8d664 (qwen3_xml parser, not touched here).
- Second test command: 68 passed.
- The new tests against main's sources: 19 failed, 241 passed. The failures are the four whole-number cases (two in test_utils.py, two in the deepseek_v4 parser test), the twelve empty-block cases in test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py (four of them for the next call in the same delta) and the three zero-cached cases (two in test_serving_chat.py, one in test_generate_stream.py).
- pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: every hook passes except check-layering, which reports vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py (platform coupling 25 -> 32) and vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (37 -> 39); this PR touches neither file, the report is the same on main c98a8d664.
- pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: passed.

End to end on our fork as in the test plan: the response's usage is {"prompt_tokens": 21, "completion_tokens": 11, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}}, i.e. the field is present with 0 for a request without a prefix-cache hit. The before and after difference for all three fixes is in the CPU tests above.

nodes.body: The new empty-block recovery mutually recurses between _skip_tool_block and _stream_current_tool_block. I reproduced a RecursionError on host 54633 using the actual parser class and a local Qwen tokenizer: start with previous_text='<tool_call>', then deliver 600 consecutive '<tool_call></tool_call>' wrappers followed by ordinary text in one delta. One and 100 wrappers return the trailing content; 600 overflow the Python stack. Speculative decoding or buffered transport can produce a large delta, so recovery needs an iterative scan and a regression covering a long burst followed by both content and a valid call. Holding this PR while preparing that correction. Audit assisted by Codex.

The iterative correction is now prepared and tested on 54633 using the actual parser and local Qwen tokenizer: 1, 100, 600 and 2000 empty blocks each followed by ordinary content or a valid weather tool call all pass (8 cases). The previous original head fails at 600. Ruff and formatting of the corrected parser pass. The integration cannot update this fork through the connected contents API (403), so the tested correction is attached below for review. This does not qualify the other changes in this frontend backport; keep the PR unmerged until its full suite passes.

```diff
--- a/vllm/tool_parsers/qwen3coder_tool_parser.py
+++ b/vllm/tool_parsers/qwen3coder_tool_parser.py
@@ -139,10 +139,19 @@
         text after it, so neither content nor later calls are lost."""
         self.skipped_tool_blocks += 1
         self.content_search_start = block_end_idx + len(self.tool_call_end_token)
-        if self._current_tool_block() < len(self._tool_start_positions(current_text)):
-            # Go on with the next block in this call: it may already be
-            # complete, and a later delta (maybe only EOS) would not get to it.
-            return self._stream_current_tool_block(current_text)
+        # A buffered/speculative delta can contain many closed empty blocks.
+        # Scan those iteratively so recovery does not consume Python frames.
+        starts = self._tool_start_positions(current_text)
+        while self._current_tool_block() < len(starts):
+            start = starts[self._current_tool_block()]
+            end = current_text.find(self.tool_call_end_token, start)
```
